issues.legal_issue: Market value of acquired land must be determined by assessing the comparability of the available sale exemplars with the acquired land, rather than relying solely on government floor-rate circulars or on the size of the transactions.

Small-plot sale exemplars may be used to determine compensation for acquired land when the land has non-agricultural potential, taking account of its location, use, and the extent held by the landowners.
A time-based escalation is not warranted when the comparable sale exemplar is close in time to the acquisition notification.
A deduction for development costs is warranted where the acquired land is used for an expressway requiring associated facilities, and the appropriate deduction in these circumstances is 25 percent.

Overpaid compensation may be recovered from similarly situated landowners, with repayment allowed in three half-yearly interest-free instalments and interest at 9 percent per annum applying to amounts not repaid within that period.
